entries.q: Fixing 'Install yet_another_config_lib_v3, version 3.6.6 or later' on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, The mod that reports this (for example Zoomify 2.15.2+1.21.11) declares a hard dependency on YetAnotherConfigLib. Add yacl {version} — if it is missing, the loader stops with 'Some of your mods are incompatible'. The file goes into the profile's Mods folder, then relaunch.

entries.q: Fixing 'Mod 'Nvidium' (nvidium) 0.4.3-beta13-1.21.11 requires version 0.8.11 or version 0.8.12 of mod 'Sodium'' on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, Nvidium and Sodium must be released in lockstep — the nvidium jar embeds an exact dependency line in its fabric.mod.json. Update both from the same source at the same time; never mix a beta Sodium with a stable Nvidium build.

entries.q: Fixing 'Mod 'Zoomify' (zoomify) - YACL still flagged after installing yet_another_config_lib_v3' on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, Three usual reasons: the YACL jar targets a different Minecraft version than Zoomify's, an older YACL 3.6.x sits lower in the folder order than the required 3.6.6, or the download was a dev build without the right fabric.mod.json. Remove every yacl jar, re-download the exact 3.6.6-plus build for your loader, relaunch.

entries.q: Fixing 'net.fabricmc.loader.impl.FormattedException: Some of your mods are incompatible with the game or each other' on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, The Fabric loader aborts at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.FormattedException before the game window opens. The lines under 'A potential solution has been determined' list the exact jar to install or replace — usually a version mismatch between Sodium, Nvidium, Zoomify and YACL on one Minecraft version.

entries.q: Fixing 'Replace mod 'Sodium' (sodium) 0.8.15-beta.1+mc1.21.11 with version 0.8.11 or version 0.8.12' on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, Beta Sodium builds break loader consistency: Nvidium 0.4.3-beta13-1.21.11 pins Sodium 0.8.11/0.8.12 and refuses the 0.8.15-beta.1 jar in the same Mods folder. entries.q: How do I fix a black screen with a cursor?
entries.a: Start with the Launcher log (Settings → Logs, or Help → Report a bug). The first line that mentions the subsystem — renderer, audio, input, network — tells you which part is actually failing. If the log is clean, try the profile's Verify files, which re-downloads the game jar.

entries.q: How do I fix Access Denied (WinError 5)?
entries.a: Windows blocked the folder the launcher wanted to write into. Run the installer once more, or move the profile storage out of a OneDrive-synced directory.

entries.q: How do I fix Ambiguous mod "X" between 1.20.1 and 1.21.x?
entries.a: Two mods in the same mod folder target different game versions. Remove one.

entries.q: How do I fix cannot use texture atlas from Sodium 0.6 in Sodium 0.5?
entries.a: Sodium was downgraded. Update Sodium inside the profile; the mods expect the newer version you just installed.

entries.q: How do I fix com.sun.jna.LastErrorException: [3]?
entries.a: Windows error 3 (path not found) while the launcher was setting up its own native libs. Reinstall the launcher build.

entries.q: How do I fix Connection refused: getsockopt?
entries.a: The server you joined is not listening on that port. Try joining through the Servers tab, which resolves the host and tells you whether the port is open.

entries.q: How do I fix Connection reset by peer?
entries.a: The server closed the connection mid-handshake, typically a firewall rule or an anti-cheat side response. Try joining the server from the vanilla client to compare.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not allocate a shared memory segment?
entries.a: On Linux, `tmpfs` for /dev/shm is too small. Increase its size in fstab or run with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` pointing at a writable location.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not create the OpenGL context (GLFW 65543)?
entries.a: Your GPU/driver does not expose OpenGL 3.3. Update the driver, or run with `MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3` on Intel to force a compatible profile.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not find bundle for org.lwjgl.opengl?
entries.a: LWJGL's module jar is missing from the profile. Press Verify files.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not find or load class com.mojang.rcl?
entries.a: Mojang changed the boot classes in the snapshot. Snapshot profiles have no mods — remove the mods and reopen the profile.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not find or load main class io.github.isolate?
entries.a: The launcher's own entry point failed, usually because the bundle was partially extracted. Reinstall from the Download page.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not find the entry-point main class?
entries.a: The game version bundled with the profile is mismatched. Press Verify files on the profile and it re-downloads the right one.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not initialize class org.lwjgl.opengles?
entries.a: An OpenGL ES context was requested when only core GL exists. Disable the mod that requested GLES, or use a normal LWJGL 3 build.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not load the launcher's own CSS?
entries.a: The asset folder was partially extracted. Reinstall from the Download page.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not reserve enough space for object heap?
entries.a: The slider is asking for more RAM than the machine physically has, or a 32-bit JVM is being squeezed for a large value. Keep the allocation within what is free in Task Manager / top.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not save profile settings: disk full?
entries.a: The drive the profile lives on is out of space. Free space or move the profile storage.

entries.q: How do I fix Could not verify session / Invalid session?
entries.a: Your Microsoft token expired and the launcher failed to renew it. Open Accounts → Sign out, sign in again and it re-authenticates.

entries.q: How do I fix Exit code -104?
entries.a: The launcher itself was killed by a policy (usually a school/enterprise endpoint-management tool). Talk to your network admin or run from home.

entries.q: How do I fix Exit code -1073740791 (0xc0000409)?
entries.a: A stack buffer check inside the JVM killed the process — almost always a shader that went fully out of memory. Remove the shader pack or lower the render distance and it stops.

entries.q: How do I fix Exit code -1073741819 (0xc0000005)?
entries.a: Access violation, which on Windows 11 typically means a stale GPU driver. Update your GPU driver from the vendor (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel) and try again.

entries.q: How do I fix Exit code -1?
entries.a: A catch-all the JVM uses when the process was terminated by the OS. On Windows, check whether an antivirus quarantined the launcher's bundled JRE; adding an exclusion for Isolate Client usually clears it.

entries.q: How do I fix Exit code 1 (generic)?
entries.a: Something inside the game threw. Open the Launcher log for the very first line of the Java stack trace — the first Caused by: is always the mod at fault.

entries.q: How do I fix Exit code 134 (SIGABRT)?
entries.a: The game asked the OS for a core dump. On Linux this usually means the GPU driver crashed the process. Update mesa or the vendor driver.

entries.q: How do I fix Exiting due to a graphics resource: DPY not found?
entries.a: The X11 display was lost mid-session (lid close, XWayland teardown). Reconnect the display and restart the session.

entries.q: How do I fix Fabric loader version X is too old for this version?
entries.a: The profile's Fabric loader predates the game version. Re-open the profile, pick the game version and let Isolate Client pick the matching loader build.

entries.q: How do I fix Failed to authenticate with Mojang (rate-limited)?
entries.a: Mojang throttles logins per IP. Wait a minute and sign in again.

entries.q: How do I fix Failed to create profile: name already in use?
entries.a: Profile names are unique. Rename or delete the old one.

entries.q: How do I fix failed to create window (wayland)?
entries.a: The AppImage needs `libwayland-client` to be present. On Ubuntu/Debian run `sudo apt install libwayland-client0`.

entries.q: How do I fix Failed to download libraries?
entries.a: The launcher could not reach Mojang's asset CDN. Check your network or try again — the next launch picks up where it left off.

entries.q: How do I fix Failed to parse the version manifest?
entries.a: Mojang's version-manifest.json changed format. Update the launcher; a shipped fix is on its way whenever Mojang breaks it.

entries.q: How do I fix Failed to query the device's GPU?
entries.a: The launcher's UI renderer got no GPU. Run with `--disable-gpu` as a one-off to confirm, then update the driver.

entries.q: How do I fix Field not found: lighter/library?
entries.a: Two mods both tried to rewrite the same field. Remove the last-added mod.

entries.q: How do I fix Game closed before the title screen appeared?
entries.a: A JVM crash very early in boot — most often a bad `JAVA_HOME` set globally from another launcher. Clear it or uninstall the other launcher.

entries.q: How do I fix IllegalArgumentException: bound must be positive?
entries.a: A mod's config file has a bad value. Reset that mod's config or remove the mod.

entries.q: How do I fix Internal error: io.netty.channel.AbstractChannel$AnnotatedConnectException?
entries.a: Bad DNS or a blocked port — most often a school/office network or a VPN. Try a different network.

entries.q: How do I fix Internal Exception: io.netty.handler.codec.DecoderException?
entries.a: A broken packet from the server or a proxy in the path. If it happens on multiple servers, the cause is your end — try turning off your VPN.

entries.q: How do I fix Iris: shader compilation error?
entries.a: A shader pack built for a different Iris/OptiFine version. Update the shader pack or update Iris inside the profile.

entries.q: How do I fix jar does not contain a fabric.mod.json?
entries.a: That jar is not a Fabric mod (it is a Forge/NeoForge jar or just a library). Remove it from the Fabric profile.

entries.q: How do I fix Java version mismatch: profile wants 8, launcher has 21?
entries.a: Old Minecraft (<=1.12.2) needs Java 8. Pick the profile's game version again — the launcher sets the correct runtime.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.ClassCastException?
entries.a: A mod is being used by code that expects a different type — the mod and the game version are out of sync. Remove the mod and see the Launcher login for the exact pair.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError?
entries.a: A static initializer inside the game or a mod threw. The first "Caused by" line in the log tells you exactly which mod.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.IllegalStateException: GLFW error 65542?
entries.a: The bundled JRE could not load OpenGL. On Linux this means the mesa/vulkan driver set used inside the launcher does not match your GPU. Install the vendor's own driver, or run with the `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=0` env var.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: net/minecraft/client/main/Main?
entries.a: The game jar itself is missing or corrupt — the launcher will re-download it if you press "Verify files" on the profile.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space?
entries.a: The game ran out of the RAM you allocated. Raise the memory slider in Profiles → Settings — or reduce the modpack size, since allocating more RAM does not fix a mod that leaks.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace?
entries.a: A mod or the modpack itself is loading too many classes. This usually means fabric-loader is older than the pack expects — update the loader inside the profile.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Unable to create native thread?
entries.a: The OS hit its per-process limit for threads. On Linux, raise `ulimit -u`; on Windows, close browser tabs (they are heavy on native threads).

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException?
entries.a: The JVM reporter for the game's main class failed. This almost always means the mod loader could not load a mod jar — check the Launcher log for the real cause.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.SecurityException: SHA1 digest error?
entries.a: The jar file's digest does not match — the download was corrupted. Delete the mod and let the launcher fetch it again.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.StackOverflowError?
entries.a: A recursive renderer (usually a modded entity or an advanced shader) went too deep. Delete the shader or the entity-heavy mod.

entries.q: How do I fix java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: liblwjgl.so?
entries.a: The LWJGL native library for your architecture is missing or the wrong arch. On ARM64 Linux, force the profile's JVM architecture if the JRE installed is the wrong bitness.

entries.q: How do I fix javaw.exe has stopped working (Windows Event 1000)?
entries.a: A game crash Windows caught. Check Reliability Monitor for the faulting path — the GPU driver and the NVIDIA overlay library are the usual names.

entries.q: How do I fix json parse error in a mod fabric.mod.json?
entries.a: A corrupt mod download. Delete the mod jar; the launcher will re-fetch it.

entries.q: How do I fix JVM crashed with exit code -805306369?
entries.a: The game's own process got a hard kill from the OS. Look in Reliability Monitor (Windows) for the exact faulting module — it is almost always the GPU driver.

entries.q: How do I fix Launch error: Tauri runtime could not start?
entries.a: GPU drivers or a headless session. Use a normal desktop session, not SSH-X.

entries.q: How do I fix Memory access fault at NVIDIA?
entries.a: The NVIDIA driver crashed the game's context. Downgrade the driver (or disable "full-screen optimizations" on the application shortcut).

entries.q: How do I fix Mismatched mod jar / Duplicate mod?
entries.a: The same mod is present in two places (Modrinth + CurseForge, or two versions in one folder). Keep one; launch again.

entries.q: How do I fix MISSING_PROFILE / MISSING_PROFILES in the auth response?
entries.a: A very rare Mojang session edge case when the account has no Java profile. Log out and back in, or check on minecraft.net whether Java Edition is actually linked to that Microsoft account.

entries.q: How do I fix Mixin apply failed?
entries.a: One mod's bytecode patch does not fit another mod's version. Remove the most recently-added mod in that profile and see if it clears.

entries.q: How do I fix mod 'X' is incompatible with mod 'Y'?
entries.a: Two mods both patch the same part of the game. Remove one; Isolate Client's own conflict checker points at the pair when it loads.

entries.q: How do I fix mod 'X' requires mod 'Y'?
entries.a: A dependency is missing. Install the required mod — Isolate Client names it with a Modrinth link when it recognises the mod.

entries.q: How do I fix Mojang javaw.cfg not found?
entries.a: The bundled JRE unpacked to a bad path. Press Verify files, or reinstall.

entries.q: How do I fix net.minecraft.client.main.Main: exit code -1073741819?
entries.a: The same access violation as above but coming out of the game itself. Update the GPU driver; on Windows 11 it is nearly always the cause.

entries.q: How do I fix night vision is inverted?
entries.a: Start with the Launcher log (Settings → Logs, or Help → Report a bug). The first line that mentions the subsystem — renderer, audio, input, network — tells you which part is actually failing. If the log is clean, try the profile's Verify files, which re-downloads the game jar.

entries.q: How do I fix NoSuchMethodError from inside the game?
entries.a: A mod was compiled against a different game version than the profile runs. Remove that mod.

entries.q: How do I fix old custom payload rejected?
entries.a: A Fabric mod is registered as a server-side channel on a server that does not accept custom packets. Remove that mod, or ask the server to allow it.

entries.q: How do I fix Out of memory rendering in Sodium?
entries.a: Sodium's off-heap buffers exceeded the process address space. Lower the render distance, disable fog, or switch the profile to 64-bit JVM only.

entries.q: How do I fix Read timed out while joining a realm?
entries.a: Realms' Microsoft AKAMAI edge was slow. Retry; this resolves itself.

entries.q: How do I fix Represented String in Mojang auth is invalid?
entries.a: Mojang's session API changed a field. Update the launcher — a fix ships within about a day.

entries.q: How do I fix Segmentation fault (exit code 139)?
entries.a: Same class of problem as SIGABRT but from an even lower layer — almost always a broken XDG/GLX setup inside the Desktop session. Test in X11 first rather than Wayland.

entries.q: How do I fix Skins don't load / default Steve?
entries.a: Mojang's `sessionserver` rate-limits skin requests per IP. Wait a minute and rejoin; if you are behind a VPN, disconnect it.

entries.q: How do I fix Sodium: shadow terrain does not support this GPU?
entries.a: Sodium's render-graph backend does not have that GPU's GL feature set. Use the "advanced" renderer option instead.

entries.q: How do I fix SSL handshake failed to launch.isolate?
entries.a: A corporate or school proxy intercepts TLS. Trust the proxy's root certificate, or use a normal network.

entries.q: How do I fix Tried to set a GUUID that already exists?
entries.a: The world has a duplicate entity. Use a world-edit/repair tool or just reload the chunk.

entries.q: How do I fix Undefined symbol in libfreetype?
entries.a: A stale system-side libfreetype got into the launcher's bundle. Reinstall; the launcher ships its own copy and does not need the system one.

entries.q: How do I fix Unsupported class file major version 65?
entries.a: A mod was built for Java 21, but the profile's JVM is older. Re-open the profile and let Isolate Client pick the correct runtime.

entries.q: How do I fix Vulkan: missing extension?
entries.a: Vulkan is not currently used by the game or the performance stack — the gl error is a red herring from another mod. See the real crash stack trace.

entries.q: How do I fix Wayland: black screen?
entries.a: Isolate Client and most Java GL games work best under XWayland. Force `__GL_YIELD=USLEEP` or launch the AppImage through `xwayland-run`.

entries.q: How do I fix Wayland: cursor disappears?
entries.a: A wayland compositor that hides the cursor off-window confuses the game's own input. Switch to XWayland for Minecraft sessions.

entries.q: How do I fix isolate: libgcc_s.so.1: version `GCC_7.0' not found?
entries.a: The OS's libgcc is older than the JRE ships. Use the .deb/AppImage for your machine, or upgrade to a distro from 2022 or later.

entries.q: How do I use the crash reporter in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Open crash reporter from the launcher's sidebar; every screen has a '?' hint in its corner. If a screen is greyed out, the profile it belongs to is busy running a session.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.12.2, why do I see a black screen with a cursor?

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21, how do I fix 'Install yet_another_config_lib_v3, version 3.6.6 or later'?
entries.a: The mod that reports this (for example Zoomify 2.15.2+1.21.11) declares a hard dependency on YetAnotherConfigLib. Add yacl {version} — if it is missing, the loader stops with 'Some of your mods are incompatible'. The file goes into the profile's Mods folder, then relaunch. On 1.21 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21, how do I fix 'Mod 'Nvidium' (nvidium) 0.4.3-beta13-1.21.11 requires version 0.8.11 or version 0.8.12 of mod 'Sodium''?
entries.a: Nvidium and Sodium must be released in lockstep — the nvidium jar embeds an exact dependency line in its fabric.mod.json. Update both from the same source at the same time; never mix a beta Sodium with a stable Nvidium build. On 1.21 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21, how do I fix 'Mod 'Zoomify' (zoomify) - YACL still flagged after installing yet_another_config_lib_v3'?
entries.a: Three usual reasons: the YACL jar targets a different Minecraft version than Zoomify's, an older YACL 3.6.x sits lower in the folder order than the required 3.6.6, or the download was a dev build without the right fabric.mod.json. Remove every yacl jar, re-download the exact 3.6.6-plus build for your loader, relaunch. On 1.21 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21, how do I fix 'Mod 'Zoomify' (zoomify) 2.15.2+1.21.11 requires version 3.6.6 or later of yet_another_config_lib_v3, which is missing'?
entries.a: This is the missing-library case: mod 'Zoomify' requires version 3.6.6 or later of yet_another_config_lib_v3, which is missing. Download the YACL jar, drop it into Mods next to Zoomify, and relaunch — no re-install of the whole profile needed. On 1.21 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21, how do I fix 'net.fabricmc.loader.impl.FormattedException: Some of your mods are incompatible with the game or each other'?
entries.a: The Fabric loader aborts at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.FormattedException before the game window opens. The lines under 'A potential solution has been determined' list the exact jar to install or replace — usually a version mismatch between Sodium, Nvidium, Zoomify and YACL on one Minecraft version. On 1.21 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21, how do I fix 'Replace mod 'Sodium' (sodium) 0.8.15-beta.1+mc1.21.11 with version 0.8.11 or version 0.8.12'?
entries.a: Beta Sodium builds break loader consistency: Nvidium 0.4.3-beta13-1.21.11 pins Sodium 0.8.11/0.8.12 and refuses the 0.8.15-beta.1 jar in the same Mods folder. Replace the Sodium jar with the matching release for your Minecraft version and the 'Incompatible mods found!' message disappears. On 1.21 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21.11, how do I fix 'Install yet_another_config_lib_v3, version 3.6.6 or later'?
entries.a: The mod that reports this (for example Zoomify 2.15.2+1.21.11) declares a hard dependency on YetAnotherConfigLib. Add yacl {version} — if it is missing, the loader stops with 'Some of your mods are incompatible'. The file goes into the profile's Mods folder, then relaunch. On 1.21.11 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21.11, how do I fix 'Mod 'Nvidium' (nvidium) 0.4.3-beta13-1.21.11 requires version 0.8.11 or version 0.8.12 of mod 'Sodium''?
entries.a: Nvidium and Sodium must be released in lockstep — the nvidium jar embeds an exact dependency line in its fabric.mod.json. Update both from the same source at the same time; never mix a beta Sodium with a stable Nvidium build. On 1.21.11 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21.11, how do I fix 'Mod 'Zoomify' (zoomify) - YACL still flagged after installing yet_another_config_lib_v3'?
entries.a: Three usual reasons: the YACL jar targets a different Minecraft version than Zoomify's, an older YACL 3.6.x sits lower in the folder order than the required 3.6.6, or the download was a dev build without the right fabric.mod.json. Remove every yacl jar, re-download the exact 3.6.6-plus build for your loader, relaunch. On 1.21.11 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21.11, how do I fix 'Mod 'Zoomify' (zoomify) 2.15.2+1.21.11 requires version 3.6.6 or later of yet_another_config_lib_v3, which is missing'?
entries.a: This is the missing-library case: mod 'Zoomify' requires version 3.6.6 or later of yet_another_config_lib_v3, which is missing. Download the YACL jar, drop it into Mods next to Zoomify, and relaunch — no re-install of the whole profile needed. On 1.21.11 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21.11, how do I fix 'net.fabricmc.loader.impl.FormattedException: Some of your mods are incompatible with the game or each other'?
entries.a: The Fabric loader aborts at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.FormattedException before the game window opens. The lines under 'A potential solution has been determined' list the exact jar to install or replace — usually a version mismatch between Sodium, Nvidium, Zoomify and YACL on one Minecraft version. On 1.21.11 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: On Minecraft 1.21.11, how do I fix 'Replace mod 'Sodium' (sodium) 0.8.15-beta.1+mc1.21.11 with version 0.8.11 or version 0.8.12'?
entries.a: Beta Sodium builds break loader consistency: Nvidium 0.4.3-beta13-1.21.11 pins Sodium 0.8.11/0.8.12 and refuses the 0.8.15-beta.1 jar in the same Mods folder. Replace the Sodium jar with the matching release for your Minecraft version and the 'Incompatible mods found!' message disappears. On 1.21.11 the same rule applies: every mod jar's fabric.mod.json must name one target MC version and agree on Sodium/YACL release lines.

entries.q: What is the crash reporter in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Collects the stack trace, OS and game version into a single pasteable report.

entries.q: What kind of telemetry does Isolate Client send on crash?
entries.a: The stack trace, the OS version, the game version, and the list of installed mods. Never the contents of chat, your account token, or any file you did not launch with.

entries.q: Why does the Fabric loader refuse to start over 'Install yet_another_config_lib_v3, version 3.6.6 or later'?

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client crash?
entries.a: Isolate Client covers crash directly — see the page section above, and the launcher's own Help screen for the in-app version of the answer.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say $GAME_DIR does not contain a valid jar?
entries.a: The game jar from the profile is missing. Use Verify files and it re-downloads from Mojang's asset CDN.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say $GAME_DIR is read-only?
entries.a: Storage permission problem. Move the profile storage out of a protected folder, or run the launcher once as the owner of that directory.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Access Denied (WinError 5)?
entries.a: Windows blocked the folder the launcher wanted to write into. Run the installer once more, or move the profile storage out of a OneDrive-synced directory.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Ambiguous mod "X" between 1.20.1 and 1.21.x?
entries.a: Two mods in the same mod folder target different game versions. Remove one.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say cannot use texture atlas from Sodium 0.6 in Sodium 0.5?
entries.a: Sodium was downgraded. Update Sodium inside the profile; the mods expect the newer version you just installed.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say com.sun.jna.LastErrorException: [3]?
entries.a: Windows error 3 (path not found) while the launcher was setting up its own native libs. Reinstall the launcher build.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Connection refused: getsockopt?
entries.a: The server you joined is not listening on that port. Try joining through the Servers tab, which resolves the host and tells you whether the port is open.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Connection reset by peer?
entries.a: The server closed the connection mid-handshake, typically a firewall rule or an anti-cheat side response. Try joining the server from the vanilla client to compare.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not allocate a shared memory segment?
entries.a: On Linux, `tmpfs` for /dev/shm is too small. Increase its size in fstab or run with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` pointing at a writable location.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not create the OpenGL context (GLFW 65543)?
entries.a: Your GPU/driver does not expose OpenGL 3.3. Update the driver, or run with `MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3` on Intel to force a compatible profile.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not find bundle for org.lwjgl.opengl?
entries.a: LWJGL's module jar is missing from the profile. Press Verify files.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not find or load class com.mojang.rcl?
entries.a: Mojang changed the boot classes in the snapshot. Snapshot profiles have no mods — remove the mods and reopen the profile.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not find or load main class io.github.isolate?
entries.a: The launcher's own entry point failed, usually because the bundle was partially extracted. Reinstall from the Download page.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not find the entry-point main class?
entries.a: The game version bundled with the profile is mismatched. Press Verify files on the profile and it re-downloads the right one.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not initialize class org.lwjgl.opengles?
entries.a: An OpenGL ES context was requested when only core GL exists. Disable the mod that requested GLES, or use a normal LWJGL 3 build.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not load the launcher's own CSS?
entries.a: The asset folder was partially extracted. Reinstall from the Download page.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not reserve enough space for object heap?
entries.a: The slider is asking for more RAM than the machine physically has, or a 32-bit JVM is being squeezed for a large value. Keep the allocation within what is free in Task Manager / top.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not save profile settings: disk full?
entries.a: The drive the profile lives on is out of space. Free space or move the profile storage.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Could not verify session / Invalid session?
entries.a: Your Microsoft token expired and the launcher failed to renew it. Open Accounts → Sign out, sign in again and it re-authenticates.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Exit code -104?
entries.a: The launcher itself was killed by a policy (usually a school/enterprise endpoint-management tool). Talk to your network admin or run from home.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Exit code -1073740791 (0xc0000409)?
entries.a: A stack buffer check inside the JVM killed the process — almost always a shader that went fully out of memory. Remove the shader pack or lower the render distance and it stops.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Exit code -1073741819 (0xc0000005)?
entries.a: Access violation, which on Windows 11 typically means a stale GPU driver. Update your GPU driver from the vendor (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel) and try again.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Exit code -1?
entries.a: A catch-all the JVM uses when the process was terminated by the OS. On Windows, check whether an antivirus quarantined the launcher's bundled JRE; adding an exclusion for Isolate Client usually clears it.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Exit code 1 (generic)?
entries.a: Something inside the game threw. Open the Launcher log for the very first line of the Java stack trace — the first Caused by: is always the mod at fault.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Exit code 134 (SIGABRT)?
entries.a: The game asked the OS for a core dump. On Linux this usually means the GPU driver crashed the process. Update mesa or the vendor driver.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Exiting due to a graphics resource: DPY not found?
entries.a: The X11 display was lost mid-session (lid close, XWayland teardown). Reconnect the display and restart the session.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Fabric loader version X is too old for this version?
entries.a: The profile's Fabric loader predates the game version. Re-open the profile, pick the game version and let Isolate Client pick the matching loader build.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Failed to authenticate with Mojang (rate-limited)?
entries.a: Mojang throttles logins per IP. Wait a minute and sign in again.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Failed to create profile: name already in use?
entries.a: Profile names are unique. Rename or delete the old one.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say failed to create window (wayland)?
entries.a: The AppImage needs `libwayland-client` to be present. On Ubuntu/Debian run `sudo apt install libwayland-client0`.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Failed to download libraries?
entries.a: The launcher could not reach Mojang's asset CDN. Check your network or try again — the next launch picks up where it left off.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Failed to parse the version manifest?
entries.a: Mojang's version-manifest.json changed format. Update the launcher; a shipped fix is on its way whenever Mojang breaks it.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Failed to query the device's GPU?
entries.a: The launcher's UI renderer got no GPU. Run with `--disable-gpu` as a one-off to confirm, then update the driver.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Field not found: lighter/library?
entries.a: Two mods both tried to rewrite the same field. Remove the last-added mod.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Game closed before the title screen appeared?
entries.a: A JVM crash very early in boot — most often a bad `JAVA_HOME` set globally from another launcher. Clear it or uninstall the other launcher.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say IllegalArgumentException: bound must be positive?
entries.a: A mod's config file has a bad value. Reset that mod's config or remove the mod.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Internal error: io.netty.channel.AbstractChannel$AnnotatedConnectException?
entries.a: Bad DNS or a blocked port — most often a school/office network or a VPN. Try a different network.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Internal Exception: io.netty.handler.codec.DecoderException?
entries.a: A broken packet from the server or a proxy in the path. If it happens on multiple servers, the cause is your end — try turning off your VPN.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Iris: shader compilation error?
entries.a: A shader pack built for a different Iris/OptiFine version. Update the shader pack or update Iris inside the profile.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say jar does not contain a fabric.mod.json?
entries.a: That jar is not a Fabric mod (it is a Forge/NeoForge jar or just a library). Remove it from the Fabric profile.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Java version mismatch: profile wants 8, launcher has 21?
entries.a: Old Minecraft (<=1.12.2) needs Java 8. Pick the profile's game version again — the launcher sets the correct runtime.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.ClassCastException?
entries.a: A mod is being used by code that expects a different type — the mod and the game version are out of sync. Remove the mod and see the Launcher login for the exact pair.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError?
entries.a: A static initializer inside the game or a mod threw. The first "Caused by" line in the log tells you exactly which mod.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.IllegalStateException: GLFW error 65542?
entries.a: The bundled JRE could not load OpenGL. On Linux this means the mesa/vulkan driver set used inside the launcher does not match your GPU. Install the vendor's own driver, or run with the `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=0` env var.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: net/minecraft/client/main/Main?
entries.a: The game jar itself is missing or corrupt — the launcher will re-download it if you press "Verify files" on the profile.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space?
entries.a: The game ran out of the RAM you allocated. Raise the memory slider in Profiles → Settings — or reduce the modpack size, since allocating more RAM does not fix a mod that leaks.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace?
entries.a: A mod or the modpack itself is loading too many classes. This usually means fabric-loader is older than the pack expects — update the loader inside the profile.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Unable to create native thread?
entries.a: The OS hit its per-process limit for threads. On Linux, raise `ulimit -u`; on Windows, close browser tabs (they are heavy on native threads).

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException?
entries.a: The JVM reporter for the game's main class failed. This almost always means the mod loader could not load a mod jar — check the Launcher log for the real cause.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.SecurityException: SHA1 digest error?
entries.a: The jar file's digest does not match — the download was corrupted. Delete the mod and let the launcher fetch it again.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.StackOverflowError?
entries.a: A recursive renderer (usually a modded entity or an advanced shader) went too deep. Delete the shader or the entity-heavy mod.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: liblwjgl.so?
entries.a: The LWJGL native library for your architecture is missing or the wrong arch. On ARM64 Linux, force the profile's JVM architecture if the JRE installed is the wrong bitness.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say javaw.exe has stopped working (Windows Event 1000)?
entries.a: A game crash Windows caught. Check Reliability Monitor for the faulting path — the GPU driver and the NVIDIA overlay library are the usual names.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say json parse error in a mod fabric.mod.json?
entries.a: A corrupt mod download. Delete the mod jar; the launcher will re-fetch it.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say JVM crashed with exit code -805306369?
entries.a: The game's own process got a hard kill from the OS. Look in Reliability Monitor (Windows) for the exact faulting module — it is almost always the GPU driver.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Launch error: Tauri runtime could not start?
entries.a: GPU drivers or a headless session. Use a normal desktop session, not SSH-X.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Memory access fault at NVIDIA?
entries.a: The NVIDIA driver crashed the game's context. Downgrade the driver (or disable "full-screen optimizations" on the application shortcut).

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Mismatched mod jar / Duplicate mod?
entries.a: The same mod is present in two places (Modrinth + CurseForge, or two versions in one folder). Keep one; launch again.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say MISSING_PROFILE / MISSING_PROFILES in the auth response?
entries.a: A very rare Mojang session edge case when the account has no Java profile. Log out and back in, or check on minecraft.net whether Java Edition is actually linked to that Microsoft account.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Mixin apply failed?
entries.a: One mod's bytecode patch does not fit another mod's version. Remove the most recently-added mod in that profile and see if it clears.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say mod 'X' is incompatible with mod 'Y'?
entries.a: Two mods both patch the same part of the game. Remove one; Isolate Client's own conflict checker points at the pair when it loads.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say mod 'X' requires mod 'Y'?
entries.a: A dependency is missing. Install the required mod — Isolate Client names it with a Modrinth link when it recognises the mod.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Mojang javaw.cfg not found?
entries.a: The bundled JRE unpacked to a bad path. Press Verify files, or reinstall.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say net.minecraft.client.main.Main: exit code -1073741819?
entries.a: The same access violation as above but coming out of the game itself. Update the GPU driver; on Windows 11 it is nearly always the cause.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say NoSuchMethodError from inside the game?
entries.a: A mod was compiled against a different game version than the profile runs. Remove that mod.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say old custom payload rejected?
entries.a: A Fabric mod is registered as a server-side channel on a server that does not accept custom packets. Remove that mod, or ask the server to allow it.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Out of memory rendering in Sodium?
entries.a: Sodium's off-heap buffers exceeded the process address space. Lower the render distance, disable fog, or switch the profile to 64-bit JVM only.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Read timed out while joining a realm?
entries.a: Realms' Microsoft AKAMAI edge was slow. Retry; this resolves itself.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Represented String in Mojang auth is invalid?
entries.a: Mojang's session API changed a field. Update the launcher — a fix ships within about a day.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Segmentation fault (exit code 139)?
entries.a: Same class of problem as SIGABRT but from an even lower layer — almost always a broken XDG/GLX setup inside the Desktop session. Test in X11 first rather than Wayland.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Skins don't load / default Steve?
entries.a: Mojang's `sessionserver` rate-limits skin requests per IP. Wait a minute and rejoin; if you are behind a VPN, disconnect it.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Sodium: shadow terrain does not support this GPU?
entries.a: Sodium's render-graph backend does not have that GPU's GL feature set. Use the "advanced" renderer option instead.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say SSL handshake failed to launch.isolate?
entries.a: A corporate or school proxy intercepts TLS. Trust the proxy's root certificate, or use a normal network.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say The asset index for that version is not yet published?
entries.a: This happens within an hour or two of a new snapshot going live. Try again later — the assets catch up.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say The Java runtime at the specified path is not a JRE?
entries.a: You pointed it at a JDK or a shell script. Clear the override and let Isolate Client use its bundled JRE.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say The profile points at a game version that no longer has a manifest?
entries.a: Mojang retired some old snapshot manifests. Delete that profile and create a new one on a supported version.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say The version you selected does not exist (or was removed)?
entries.a: Some very old alpha/beta manifests were retired by Mojang.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Tried to set a GUUID that already exists?
entries.a: The world has a duplicate entity. Use a world-edit/repair tool or just reload the chunk.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Undefined symbol in libfreetype?
entries.a: A stale system-side libfreetype got into the launcher's bundle. Reinstall; the launcher ships its own copy and does not need the system one.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Unsupported class file major version 65?
entries.a: A mod was built for Java 21, but the profile's JVM is older. Re-open the profile and let Isolate Client pick the correct runtime.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Vulkan: missing extension?
entries.a: Vulkan is not currently used by the game or the performance stack — the gl error is a red herring from another mod. See the real crash stack trace.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Wayland: black screen?
entries.a: Isolate Client and most Java GL games work best under XWayland. Force `__GL_YIELD=USLEEP` or launch the AppImage through `xwayland-run`.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say Wayland: cursor disappears?
entries.a: A wayland compositor that hides the cursor off-window confuses the game's own input. Switch to XWayland for Minecraft sessions.

entries.q: Why does Isolate Client say isolate: libgcc_s.so.1: version `GCC_7.0' not found?
entries.a: The OS's libgcc is older than the JRE ships. Use the .deb/AppImage for your machine, or upgrade to a distro from 2022 or later.

entries.q: Why is Isolate Client showing a black screen?
entries.a: Isolate Client covers screen directly — see the page section above, and the launcher's own Help screen for the in-app version of the answer.

entries.q: Why is Isolate Client showing a white screen?
entries.a: Isolate Client covers screen directly — see the page section above, and the launcher's own Help screen for the in-app version of the answer.

entries.q: Why is Isolate Client stuck on the loading screen?
entries.a: Isolate Client covers stuck directly — see the page section above, and the launcher's own Help screen for the in-app version of the answer.

entries.q: Why won't Isolate Client launch?
entries.a: Isolate Client covers launching directly — see the page section above, and the launcher's own Help screen for the in-app version of the answer.

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash and the log is empty?
entries.a: the JVM died before writing anything. Reproduce with the vanilla launcher to see whether it is Isolate Client-specific

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash at 99% of world loading?
entries.a: almost always a chunk-write failure — check the disk's free space

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash at the title screen?
entries.a: a mod at boot crashed before the title screen showed. Delete the most recently added jar

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash during world generation?
entries.a: a mod changed the worldgen without registering the seed. Remove the mod or start a new world

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash on entering a boat/minecart?
entries.a: a vehicle mod is incompatible with the game version; remove it

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash on opening the inventory?
entries.a: a mod that adds an inventory slot is out of date or conflicts with another

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash on server join?
entries.a: the server's version does not match yours — check with the server's staff which version they run

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash on world load?
entries.a: the world was saved by a newer game version; up-convert it in the vanilla launcher

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash when opening the creative menu?
entries.a: a mod has a bad item registration. Remove the newest mod or update it

entries.q: Isolate Client on Minecraft 1.10.2: crash when saving?
entries.a: the disk is out of space, or the world file has a bad chunk — back up and run a region-file repair tool

entries.q: Isolate Client says: Install yet_another_config_lib_v3, version 3.6.6 or later — what do I do?
entries.a: The mod that reports this (for example Zoomify 2.15.2+1.21.11) declares a hard dependency on YetAnotherConfigLib. Add yacl {version} — if it is missing, the loader stops with 'Some of your mods are incompatible'. The file goes into the profile's Mods folder, then relaunch. Isolate Client's Mods screen flags these mismatches before launch with the same advice, and the profile's Verify files re-pins the official mod set.

entries.q: Isolate Client says: Mod 'Nvidium' (nvidium) 0.4.3-beta13-1.21.11 requires version 0.8.11 or version 0.8.12 of mod 'Sodium' — what do I do?
entries.a: Nvidium and Sodium must be released in lockstep — the nvidium jar embeds an exact dependency line in its fabric.mod.json. Update both from the same source at the same time; never mix a beta Sodium with a stable Nvidium build. Isolate Client's Mods screen flags these mismatches before launch with the same advice, and the profile's Verify files re-pins the official mod set.

entries.q: Isolate Client says: Mod 'Zoomify' (zoomify) - YACL still flagged after installing yet_another_config_lib_v3 — what do I do?
entries.a: Three usual reasons: the YACL jar targets a different Minecraft version than Zoomify's, an older YACL 3.6.x sits lower in the folder order than the required 3.6.6, or the download was a dev build without the right fabric.mod.json. Remove every yacl jar, re-download the exact 3.6.6-plus build for your loader, relaunch. Isolate Client's Mods screen flags these mismatches before launch with the same advice, and the profile's Verify files re-pins the official mod set.

entries.q: Isolate Client says: Mod 'Zoomify' (zoomify) 2.15.2+1.21.11 requires version 3.6.6 or later of yet_another_config_lib_v3, which is missing — what do I do?
entries.a: This is the missing-library case: mod 'Zoomify' requires version 3.6.6 or later of yet_another_config_lib_v3, which is missing. Download the YACL jar, drop it into Mods next to Zoomify, and relaunch — no re-install of the whole profile needed. Isolate Client's Mods screen flags these mismatches before launch with the same advice, and the profile's Verify files re-pins the official mod set.

entries.q: Isolate Client says: net.fabricmc.loader.impl.FormattedException: Some of your mods are incompatible with the game or each other — what do I do?
entries.a: The Fabric loader aborts at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.FormattedException before the game window opens. The lines under 'A potential solution has been determined' list the exact jar to install or replace — usually a version mismatch between Sodium, Nvidium, Zoomify and YACL on one Minecraft version. Isolate Client's Mods screen flags these mismatches before launch with the same advice, and the profile's Verify files re-pins the official mod set.

entries.q: Isolate Client says: Replace mod 'Sodium' (sodium) 0.8.15-beta.1+mc1.21.11 with version 0.8.11 or version 0.8.12 — what do I do?
entries.a: Beta Sodium builds break loader consistency: Nvidium 0.4.3-beta13-1.21.11 pins Sodium 0.8.11/0.8.12 and refuses the 0.8.15-beta.1 jar in the same Mods folder. Replace the Sodium jar with the matching release for your Minecraft version and the 'Incompatible mods found!' message disappears. Isolate Client's Mods screen flags these mismatches before launch with the same advice, and the profile's Verify files re-pins the official mod set.

entries.q: isolate: libgcc_s.so.1: version `GCC_7.0' not found on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, The OS's libgcc is older than the JRE ships. Use the .deb/AppImage for your machine, or upgrade to a distro from 2022 or later.

entries.q: Does the AppImage need `fuse` on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, Newer kernels ship FUSE 3, which is what AppImages link against. If yours is older, use the .deb instead — or `appimage-exec` / `fuse3` for the desktop entry.

entries.q: Does Isolate Client contain malware?
entries.a: No. Every build is a plain Tauri bundle you download directly from GitHub Releases, signed and hashed. Nothing in Isolate Client collects more than crash/analytics events, and none of that includes your session cookie.

entries.q: Does Isolate Client cost FPS on Minecraft 1.10.2?
entries.a: Minecraft 1.10.2 — No. The launcher itself is not in the game loop; the bundled performance mods *increase* FPS. The UI closes out of the game process's memory once the client is running.

entries.q: Is my Microsoft account password stored anywhere on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, No. Login uses Microsoft's standard device-code OAuth, which returns a session-only token stored encrypted on your OS keychain path (Windows Credential Store / libsecret). Log out any time from Accounts → Sign out.

entries.q: Is there a portable Linux install on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, Yes — the AppImage is fully portable and runs from any directory, including from a USB stick. Your profile data follows `$HOME` though, so for a truly portable setup set `$XDG_DATA_HOME` before launching.

entries.q: What is Isolate Client?
entries.a: Isolate Client is a free, lightweight Minecraft launcher built for performance. It bundles proven Fabric performance mods (Sodium, Lithium, FerriteCore and friends), so a fresh install already runs faster than vanilla — and you can add your own mods on top.

entries.q: What kind of telemetry does Isolate Client send on crash on a Steam Deck?
entries.a: On a Steam Deck, The stack trace, the OS version, the game version, and the list of installed mods. Never the contents of chat, your account token, or any file you did not launch with.

entries.q: What ports does Isolate Client use?
entries.a: HTTPS (443) to our API, to GitHub for releases, and Mojang's authentication. And to the server you are joining — typically 25565 over TCP.

entries.q: Does the AppImage need `fuse`?
entries.a: Newer kernels ship FUSE 3, which is what AppImages link against. If yours is older, use the .deb instead — or `appimage-exec` / `fuse3` for the desktop entry.

entries.q: Does Isolate Client have a portable Windows version?
entries.a: A `.zip` build without an installer is planned but not yet published; the .exe installer is the currently supported Windows install method.

entries.q: How big is the installer?
entries.a: Windows ~65 MB compressed; Linux AppImage ~60 MB. The bundled performance mods add another ~9 MB once the profile is created.

entries.q: How do I completely uninstall Isolate Client?
entries.a: Windows: Settings → Apps → Isolate Client → Uninstall. Linux: `rm -rf $XDG_DATA_HOME/Isolate Client` plus `~/.local/share/applications/isolate.desktop` and the AppImage file itself.

entries.q: Do I need Java separately?
entries.a: No. Isolate Client ships a bundled, correctly-patched JRE for each Minecraft version so the game always runs with the right runtime version.

entries.q: Does the Java picker cost FPS?
entries.a: Launcher-side screens are not part of the game's process — the Java picker costs zero in-game framerate. Only in-game mods affect FPS.

entries.q: How do I use the Java picker in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Open Java picker from the launcher's sidebar; every screen has a '?' hint in its corner. If a screen is greyed out, the profile it belongs to is busy running a session.

entries.q: Is the Java picker free in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Isolate Client is free as a whole; nothing inside the launcher is behind a paywall. The only paid items in the whole product are optional cosmetics on the Store.

entries.q: What is the Java picker in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Choose which runtime a profile uses — the bundled one is recommended.

entries.q: Does the theme switcher cost FPS?

entries.q: How do I use the theme switcher in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Open theme switcher from the launcher's sidebar; every screen has a '?' hint in its corner. If a screen is greyed out, the profile it belongs to is busy running a session.

entries.q: Is the theme switcher free in Isolate Client?

entries.q: Does Quark work in Isolate Client?

entries.q: Does Quark work on multiplayer servers?
entries.a: It depends on whether Quark is client-only. Rendering mods are always fine; gameplay mods usually need the server to also have the matching server-side plugin or mod installed.

entries.q: Does Quark work on older Minecraft versions?
entries.a: Most mods publish builds for several game versions. Check that Quark's recommended file list covers the version in your profile.

entries.q: Does Quark work with the bundled performance stack?
entries.a: The bundled stack is Sodium + Lithium + FerriteCore + Iris. Quark is designed to work alongside those when the versions match — Isolate Client's conflict checker will tell you if one is out of date.

entries.q: Does Isolate Client support custom resource packs?
entries.a: Yes. Drop a .zip into the profile's `resourcepacks/` folder or drag it into the Resource Packs screen in the launcher.

entries.q: Does Isolate Client support Fabric?
entries.a: Yes, and it is the default loader for the bundled performance stack.

entries.q: Does Isolate Client work with CurseForge modpacks?
entries.a: Not yet. CurseForge packs ship a manifest with mod IDs that need their API to resolve. For .zip packs that ship the actual .jar files (MultiMC-style), use Profiles → Import.

entries.q: How do I add mods in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Isolate Client covers mods directly — see the page section above, and the launcher's own Help screen for the in-app version of the answer.

entries.q: How do I add mods?
entries.a: Open Isolate Client → Profiles → pick the profile → Mods → drag in .jar files. Isolate Client checks loader compatibility, shows version collisions and never puts an incompatible jar in a fabric profile.

entries.q: How do I install /gamemode-integrating Fabric Command API in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Profiles → pick the profile → Mods → drop in the /gamemode-integrating Fabric Command API .jar. Isolate Client checks the loader and the game version, and tells you if it needs a dependency like Fabric API.

entries.q: How do I update mods?
entries.a: Open the profile's Mods tab; newer versions of a mod you have already installed show an update indicator. Modpack updates preserve custom options.txt unless you ask otherwise.

entries.q: How do I use the Mods screen in Isolate Client?
entries.a: Open Mods screen from the launcher's sidebar; every screen has a '?' hint in its corner. If a screen is greyed out, the profile it belongs to is busy running a session.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.10.2?
entries.a: Vanilla/Forge; Fabric does not target 1.10. Import from another launcher is cleaner here than a fresh install.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.11.2?
entries.a: Vanilla or Forge; Fabric does not target 1.11. Performance mods are mostly server-side mods at this version.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.12.2?
entries.a: Forge, or Vanilla with legacy patches. Fabric's modern line starts at 1.14. The biggest modpack ecosystem for Forge is here.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.14.4?
entries.a: Fabric — the first version Sodium's modern stack targets. Sodium 0.1/0.2 (early) is where the stack started.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.15.2?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium The bundled performance stack works well here.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.16.1?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium + Lithium The official 1.16.x line Sodium still supports.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.16.5?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium (widely used) — this is the most common 1.16 pick. Almost every 1.16 modpack targets 1.16.5.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.17.1?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium First version that needs Java 17 — Isolate Client bundles it.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.18.1?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium Isolate Client handles the Java 17 runtime automatically.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.18.2?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium — the standard 1.18 pick. Almost all 1.18 mods target this version.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.19.2?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium — most 1.19 mods are here. 1.19.3/4 have thinner mod coverage.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.19.4?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium; some mods only publish 1.19.4. A narrow window of mod availability in this version.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.20.1?
entries.a: Fabric and NeoForge both work; the largest 1.20 mod ecosystem. Most new Fabric mods still publish for 1.20.1 as well as 1.21.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.20.4?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium; thinner mod coverage than 1.20.1. Pick this when you want the newest engine features with fewer mods.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.20.6?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium; the last stop of 1.20. Even narrower mod coverage than 1.20.4.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.21.1?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium — the current mod-ecosystem centre of gravity. NeoForge also supports this version.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.21.4?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium with the newest engine features. Some popular mods are not here yet, so check your mod list.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.21.8?
entries.a: Fabric + Sodium — the newest supported line. Mod coverage is the thinnest; most mods are on 1.21.1.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.7.10?
entries.a: Vanilla, or legacy Forge; Fabric 1.x does not cover 1.7. MultiMC-style profiles from other launchers import cleanly.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.8.9?
entries.a: Vanilla or OptiFine-style legacy patch; modern Fabric does not target this version. PvP players usually run a 1.8.9-specific patch-mod.

entries.q: What mods are available on Minecraft 1.9.4?
entries.a: Vanilla; the Fabric loader does not cover early 1.9. Use the Vanilla loader and a Legacy mod if you want modern patches.

entries.q: Does the offline mode cost FPS?

entries.q: Does Isolate Client cost FPS?
entries.a: No. The launcher itself is not in the game loop; the bundled performance mods *increase* FPS. The UI closes out of the game process's memory once the client is running.

entries.q: Why is my ping on CrimeCity worse with Isolate Client?
entries.a: It shouldn't be. If you notice it, check that Krypton or another network optimization mod was not removed — removing it causes more GC pauses, not worse ping. {srv} latency is your route distance, which no launcher changes.
